discharge_notes.text:
Name:  ___                  Unit No:   ___
 
Admission Date:  ___              Discharge Date:   ___
 
Date of Birth:  ___             Sex:   M
 
Service: MEDICINE
 
Allergies: 
Patient recorded as having No Known Allergies to Drugs
 
Attending: ___.
 
Chief Complaint:
Chest Pain, Trunk Rash
 
Major Surgical or Invasive Procedure:
none

 
History of Present Illness:
Mr. ___ is a ___ year-old man with PMH of HTN, asthma, HCV 
(cleared), polysubstance abuse (prior heroin use, active 
marijuana, cocaine, & alcohol), with CAD s/p multiple PCIs and 
stents to OM2 x 2 and PL x 1, and active cocaine use (denies use 
within 3 weeks, but +tox screen in ED) who presents to the ER w/ 
two days of substernal CP. CP is non-radiating, non-exertional, 
occurs at rest, lasts seconds to 15min. No association with 
position, coughing. Patient reports + diaphoresis and SOB 
associated with CP. He denies n/v associated with CP. He reports 
pain is ___ at its worst. He reports no exacerbating/ 
alleviating factors. Patient denies cocaine use recently (last 
use ""a few"" weeks ago"") but + urine tox screen for cocaine in 
ED. 

The patient also c/o worsening rash on b/l thigh legs for about 
1 week which has spread to periumbilicus & foreskin. No known 
exposures. He notes marked pruritis.  
Prior to presenting to pt drank 3 beers and smoked marijuana. 
Denies cocaine use within the past few weeks (but +tox screen, 
as above).  
.  
In ED, VS 97.8, 91, 142/98, 18, 99% on RA. EKG abnormal at 
baseline; no new changes. Nml CXR. Urine tox positive for 
cocaine & opiates (had already gotten the latter in the ED), and 
alcohol 127. CP was relieved w/ morhpine (unclear if nitro 
helped).  
.  
On arrival to ward, the patient complained of ___ CP and mild 
SOB. Also, he complained of significant discomfort over rash on 
thighs ___ pruritis. The patient was given 4mg morphine & 
resolution of pain.  
.  
ROS: + recent cold for the past ___ weeks with poor po intake 
over the past several days, nausea, and vomiting x ___ yesterday. 
No diarrhea. +occasional headaches esp w/ nitro. + muscle cramps 
in legs and back x a few weeks, worse at night. No cough, SOB, 
f/c, dysuria or hematuria, abd pain. CV as above.  
 
Past Medical History:
 - HTN  
- polysubstance abuse: cocaine last used ""few weeks ago"

There are low lung volumes.  Allowing for this, cardiac and mediastinal
contours appear unremarkable.  Pulmonary vascularity is within normal limits.
